messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: paging: high error rate observed for /v1/console/model-status across us-west-2. Trigger: 5xx > 5% for 3m. Pager routed to oncall.
Alice Mendez: I’m oncall — looking. First check: is this console failing to load model metadata or is the control plane rejecting requests?
Raj Patel: jumping in. Data plane (inference) metrics look normal for the same time window. Latency and tokens/sec are fine. Errors are only from Console API path hitting 500s.
Mei Chen: can you paste a sample 500 response body? might be a config lookup error.
Ben Ortiz: customer-facing: Claire — any reports?
Claire Gomez: we've got a support ticket from Acme with console errors since ~13:07 UTC, they can’t list model versions in the UI. They say inference still works via API.
Tom Li: that matches: API key routes still returning completions. So divergence between control plane (console /model endpoints) and dataplane.
Alice Mendez: hypothesis 1: config propagation job failed after deploy and console service is reading stale/partial config causing NPE. Hypothesis 2: a feature flag rollout for schema enforcement hit console only.
Raj Patel: checking pods: console-frontend shows 502/500 logs around 13:06. Controller logs show `KeyError: 'model_defaults'` in config loader. Pushing grep: 
```
2026-03-12T13:06:22Z console ERROR KeyError 'model_defaults' at config_loader.py:88
2026-03-12T13:06:22Z controller WARN config-sync failed for cluster us-west-2
```
Alice Mendez: thanks. Who rolled config ~13:00? Ben?
Ben Ortiz: Wasn't me. I see a config publish task from automation at 12:58 (auto-sync job). Maybe last deploy triggered a partial state.
Mei Chen: sounds like config-sync failure. Could be the flag gating for new schema. OpsBot, any recent feature-flag changes?
OpsBot: feature-flag-change: `console_schema_strictness` -> enabled for 50% on 2026-03-12T12:59:01Z by rollout-service (id: rr-8492).
Tom Li: oh — that flag would make console require `model_defaults` to exist. If config-sync missed a key, that would raise KeyError. Data plane probably tolerant.
Alice Mendez: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable rollout for `console_schema_strictness` 2) force full config re-sync for us-west-2 3) continue customer comms. Who can flip flag now?
Raj Patel: I can rollback the rollout to 0% now. Doing: `rolloutctl set rr-8492 0`
Raj Patel: (4s) done. rollout-service responded 200.
Mei Chen: initiating config resync: `configsync --region us-west-2 --full` — kicking now.
Ben Ortiz: Claire, tell Acme support we’re mitigating, ETA ~10min, will follow up with timeline and RCA. :thumbsup:
Claire Gomez: on it — posted in ticket and Slack DM.
Raj Patel: console pods are still erroring but new logs show fewer KeyErrors. Controller shows resync started and fetching latest config.
Tom Li: I’m seeing model listing in console for a subset of users — gradual improvement.
Alice Mendez: monitoring: set threshold alert muted to avoid noise, keep this thread for timeline.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation applied: flag rollback + config resync at 1793000150. Current severity: degraded, impact: console list/metadata failures for some users, dataplane unaffected.
Mei Chen: resync complete log: 
```
2026-03-12T13:12:05Z configsync INFO full sync finished, applied 312 entries
2026-03-12T13:12:06Z controller INFO reconcile finished for us-west-2
```
Raj Patel: console 5xx rate dropped from 6.1% -> 0.8% over 2 minutes.
Alice Mendez: moving to handoff in 20m. I’ll prepare a timeline for the oncall-to-oncall pass. Key facts: deploy/rollout started 12:59, errors at ~13:06, mitigation at ~13:10, resync finished 13:12, impact window ~13:06–13:14.
Ben Ortiz: logging for RCA: need to surface that rollout-service allowed console-strictness to target control-plane components only — looks like the flag was mis-scoped to include console microservice but not controller, resulting in partial enforcement.
Tom Li: add note: data plane tolerant because inference code reads defaults client-side if absent, console trusts config server.
Claire Gomez: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~2% of active orgs saw missing model lists, 1 high-touch enterprise (Acme) raised ticket. No data lost.
Alice Mendez: handoff to next oncall (Raj -> Mei): Raj, you stay for 10m overlap. Mei, you take primary after that and own RCA follow-up.
Raj Patel: will stay. Also uploading logs bundle to incident bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1793009999/logs.tar.gz` (contains console/controller logs).
Mei Chen: captured config snapshot: `s3://redwood-incidents/1793009999/config_snapshot.json` and rollout metadata `rr-8492` details.
Alice Mendez: next steps in RCA thread: 1) reproduce scoping bug locally 2) add fail-safe in console for missing keys (graceful fallback) 3) improve rollout scoping checks to cross-verify affected services list 4) customer comms draft. Assign owners and ETA.
Ben Ortiz: I'll own comms draft, ETA 2h.
Tom Li: I'll take #2 (console fallback) — aim PR today.
Raj Patel: I'll take #1 and upload reproduction steps.
Mei Chen: I'll take #3, check rollout-service policy engine.
Claire Gomez: I’ll draft customer note and get legal if needed.
Alice Mendez: thanks everyone. Tagging incident-bot to mark this thread as mitigation-complete when stable for 30m. Planning follow-up RCA meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
incident-bot: NOTE: mitigation observed stable for 30m window starting at 1793010150 -> will auto-close incident-proactive alert if no regressions.
